channel.title: Echo's Reading Feed
channel.description: Curated reading lists: how live events and esports get made. Items marked [recommended] are the picks.

item.title: [recommended] I Am with You: The Active Love of Samwise Gamgee
item.description: Fellowship & Fairydust - Sam's devotion to Frodo is framed as a choice made again and again, not a mood, which is the closest literary version of "I'll do whatever it takes to keep you going."

item.title: [recommended] 'I am the Resurrection and the Life': Sydney Carton, Love and Redemption
item.description: National Catholic Register - Carton gives up his life so the woman he loves can live happily with someone else. It is the purest case of one person's cost making another's thriving possible.

item.title: [recommended] Shadow of the Colossus: What would you do for someone you love?
item.description: Hypercritic - Wander gives everything, eventually himself, to bring one girl back. It asks directly what devotion costs and whether the cost is worth it.

item.title: [recommended] Love is a Game: Ico Revisited
item.description: digital love child - A personal essay on how the author's read of Ico changed between 15 and 25: holding someone's hand through a labyrinth as the whole point of the game.

item.title: [recommended] Life, Death, Sacrifice: The Beautiful Tragedies of Nier: Automata
item.description: VICE - The game's later endings turn on characters choosing to lose something so others can go on. The piece is about sacrifice as the thing that makes a life matter.

item.title: [recommended] Nier: Automata - True Kindness in Games Requires Sacrifice
item.description: iThrive Games Foundation - Argues that the game's kindest acts are the ones that cost the player something, which maps onto devotion that has a real price.

item.title: [recommended] What Love Really Means: Iris Murdoch on Unselfing
item.description: The Marginalian - Murdoch's idea of love as unselfing, seeing someone as fully real, is the philosophical root of "I'd rather see you thrive than center myself."

item.title: [recommended] Love is the extremely difficult realisation that something other than oneself is real
item.description: The Irish Times - A newspaper essay that takes Murdoch's line seriously and argues real love is about the other person, not the feeling.

item.title: [recommended] The Sacrament of Attention
item.description: Wayfare - Attention is where devotion shows up first: what you give your full attention to is what you serve.

item.title: [recommended] Your attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity
item.description: Centre for Public Christianity - Simone Weil's claim that attending to another person is the purest generosity, which is a quieter version of devotion than your quote's.

item.title: [recommended] Love is like a tree: Works of Love, Chapter I
item.description: Random Numbers - Kierkegaard's idea that love is a duty you choose, not a feeling that happens to you, close to the "I will do whatever it is" side of your quote.

item.title: [recommended] Kenosis and Self-Love
item.description: Sean Reagan - Self-emptying as a way of loving, paired with an honest look at what loving yourself means. A useful counterweight inside the same essay.

item.title: [recommended] The loves that don't get roses
item.description: Sara Engram - Everyday devotion with no applause: lifting someone from bed to wheelchair, repeating the same story five times. Love as unglamorous cost.

item.title: [recommended] The Sacred Act of Caregiving
item.description: Megan Shen - Treats the tireless, unrewarded work of care as sacred, and says who keeps the ship afloat.

item.title: [recommended] The Sacred Side of Caregiving: Finding Honor in the Hardest Work of Love
item.description: This Part - A spouse reading marriage vows in sickness and in health as a daily, unseen, holy kind of devotion.

item.title: [recommended] The Life, Death, and Resurrection of Caregiving
item.description: Mothering Spirit - Being awakened many times for love of someone who cannot care for themselves, and the paradox of finding grace in that.

item.title: [recommended] Oh, the Beautiful Things I Long to Give You!
item.description: The Way Back to Ourselves - A parent looking at a sleeping child and wanting to give them everything. Devotion as longing for someone else's good.

item.title: [recommended] Notes on devotion
item.description: A Life Well Loved - Devotion as the boldest, most beautiful act of rebellion in an age of endless choice. It asks you to narrow your world so your roots go deeper.

item.title: [recommended] Why I Refuse to Live Only for Myself
item.description: G'DayMZ - Pushes back on "do it for you" culture and says her path exists because of people who gave for her.

item.title: [recommended] Les Miserables
item.description: Refuge & Ruins - Valjean as a man who understands what sacrifice and surrender demand, and who gives up control to love well.

item.title: [recommended] The Four Loves, Chapter 6: Charity
item.description: Restless Pilgrim - C.S. Lewis on gift-love and how natural love can become too much, with excerpts and notes. Directly about the weight and danger of giving yourself away.

item.title: [recommended] Love
item.description: Frederick Buechner - Love as the most powerful and most powerless force, because it can only be given, never forced. Short and quotable.

item.title: Well done, Sam Gamgee
item.description: Prism Magazine - A short note pointing to Hannah Holder's article on Sam's humility and willingness to die for Frodo.

item.title: Rilke on the Relationship Between Solitude, Love, Sex, and Creativity
item.description: The Marginalian - Rilke's idea that love is two solitudes protecting and greeting each other, which complements all-in devotion.

item.title: [recommended] Violet Evergarden: (Sacrificial) Love and Its Power to Empower
item.description: SOLA Network - The anime's major, who loves Violet by giving her a life of her own. Sacrificial love that empowers the other person.

item.title: The Giving Tree of Motherhood
item.description: Desiring God - A mother finds her love poured out in small daily ways, with joy in it, and ties the Giving Tree to that.

item.title: Losing my life
item.description: a way of seeing - Frames love as sacrifice in a religious way and says she's not a doormat, but leans toward unconditional giving. Read with some distance.

item.title: I Live My Life For You
item.description: Vivodoc - Strong "live for others" register. Read with some distance, as it leans toward radical altruism with little attention to cost.

item.title: I would live for you
item.description: zanealmond (Medium) - Contains talk of dying and suicide. It argues that living is the harder, braver act.

item.title: Somebody Still Needs To Be Loved By You
item.description: Jocelyn Ulevicus - Contains the author's story of surviving suicide and staying for people who love her. Heavy.

item.title: The Line Between Self-Gift and Self-Erasure
item.description: Other Feminisms - Asks where giving yourself away turns into disappearing, using Sara Ruddick on maternal work.

item.title: Against Selfless Love
item.description: Carescapes - Questions "selflessness" as a compliment and what it hides.

item.title: What 'The Giving Tree' Gets Wrong About Love and Happiness
item.description: Psychology Today - The tree gives everything and is "happy," and the author now thinks this misreads love.

item.title: Can You Love Someone Without Losing Yourself?
item.description: hasif - Love changes you and their happiness starts to matter more, but there is a difference between being part of a life and being the center it turns on.

item.title: Charlotte, Wilbur, and the myth of the selfless mentor
item.description: Chronicle of Evidence-Based Mentoring - Asks why volunteer mentors give time and emotional energy, and says selflessness is a myth.

item.title: [recommended] Believe In Others
item.description: Paul Millerd - The closest match: people who raise another person's ambitions before success is visible.

item.title: [recommended] Seeing Possibilities - The Donella Meadows Project
item.description: Elizabeth Sawin - A parent's task to reflect a child's potential becomes a way of believing in humanity.

item.title: [recommended] Believing in people as a conscious act of rebellion
item.description: The Nomadic ADHD Coach - Believing in people is a deliberate rebellion against a culture of fault-finding.

item.title: [recommended] How to be your friend's #1 fan
item.description: Erin Greenawald - A thoughtful guide to noticing and celebrating the work friends quietly care about.

item.title: [recommended] Mudita. The practice of sympathetic joy.
item.description: Andrea Scher - A blogger discovers that celebrating other people's victories makes her own heart feel full.

item.title: [recommended] The secret to happiness? Finding joy in others.
item.description: Nadine Levy - Her realization: she does not have to be the center of her own happiness.

item.title: [recommended] The blessing of cheering people on
item.description: Joe Pagetta - "Balcony people" lift others up with real encouragement instead of automatic judgment.

item.title: [recommended] Sympathetic Joy
item.description: Sharon Salzberg - Treat others' happiness as a source of your own, rather than a limited resource.

item.title: [recommended] RISE: The Value of Believing in Someone
item.description: Jennifer L. Keluskar - Explains what your belief can do for the person receiving it.

item.title: [recommended] What Archbishop Tutu's ubuntu credo teaches the world about justice and harmony
item.description: Thaddeus Metz - A philosophical frame for why helping others flourish can feel deeply human.

item.title: [recommended] 2013 Convocation Address
item.description: George Saunders - A moving speech about becoming less self-centered and more loving without abandoning your ambitions.

item.title: [recommended] Alain de Botton on Emotional Generosity and the Difficult, Largehearted Art of Charity of Interpretation
item.description: Maria Popova - Believing in people can mean allowing room for growth even when they are imperfect.

item.title: [recommended] Mudita: The Buddha's Teaching on Unselfish Joy
item.description: Nyanaponika Thera and contributors - A whole collection about why shared joy and support are natural capacities worth developing.

item.title: [adjacent] Be Someone People Can Root For
item.description: Paul Millerd - The other side of the feeling: letting people see your hopes so they can root for you.

item.title: [adjacent] Mudita is not "sympathetic joy"
item.description: Bodhipaksa - A narrower view: celebrate the good qualities and actions that help people flourish, not every kind of success.

item.title: [adjacent] Root for Your Friends · Joseph Thacker
item.description: Joseph Thacker - Rooting for friends creates a shared upward spiral, not a competition.

item.title: [recommended] Championing: the worthwhile risk of believing in people out loud - Nick Robinson
item.description: Nick Robinson - A name for the active part: championing is believing in people out loud.

item.title: [adjacent] The Case for Creative Generosity
item.description: Richard Holman - Find pleasure in where someone else can take an idea you shared.

item.title: [adjacent] Believing in People – Gary Blog
item.description: Gary Ong - People are more than resources on a project chart.

item.title: [adjacent] I Believe in You – GBShaw Blog
item.description: GBShaw Blog - A former vicar argues that faith in people is an overlooked kind of faith.

item.title: [adjacent] I Believe in People
item.description: Stuck in the Middle with You - An obscure personal blogger chooses to believe in people without claiming certainty about everything they believe.

item.title: [recommended] Mudita (Sympathetic Joy): The Most Difficult Brahma-Vihara to Cultivate
item.description: Sam Woolfe - Explores why genuine joy for others can become difficult even when we want it.

item.title: [recommended] Mudita for Yourself? Yes, Definitely!
item.description: Jill Shepherd and Leigh Brasington - Shared joy can include your own flourishing too.

item.title: [recommended] Muditā: Intention Beyond Selectivity - by Kasia Murfet
item.description: Kasia Murfet - A small beach scene becomes a reflection on opening to strangers' happiness.

item.title: [recommended] Finding joy in others' happiness
item.description: T. Elizabeth Bell - A writer takes joy in engagements, creative breakthroughs and a well-earned prize.

item.title: [recommended] Be a fan of your friends
item.description: Peachkit - Being a fan of friends gives a musician the energy to keep showing up.

item.title: [recommended] Being Fans of Each Other – Roll for Joy
item.description: Rory the Dungeon Master Pastor - At a gaming table, rooting for each other turns success into a shared story.

item.title: [recommended] The Sweet and Bitter Gifts of Seeing Potential in others
item.description: Jamie Lee - A valuable counterpoint: your picture of someone's potential must not become a demand.

item.title: [recommended] Why I believe in people. – @visakanv's archives
item.description: Visakan Veerasamy - Believing in yourself and believing in others can come from the same respect for human possibility.

item.title: [recommended] The joys of mentorship
item.description: Dorothy Anne - A funny personal account of how much joy and learning the mentor gets back.

item.title: [recommended] The True Meaning of Mentorship
item.description: Norman Winarsky - A eulogy remembers someone who saw a young person's potential and changed the shape of his life.

item.title: [recommended] Tell Me Your Hopes and Dreams
item.description: Rona Maynard - A mentor first asks about her hopes and dreams; decades later she does the same for another writer.

item.title: [recommended] Electric Zoo Part 3 - Load Out
item.description: Kelly Levstek (SoundGirls) - A storm-canceled festival turns into a muddy overnight strike, with too few hands, tangled cables and several departments trying to pack at once.

item.title: [recommended] A gaming event in a League of its own
item.description: Tristan Greaves (Tech Interrupt) - Backstage tour of the Worlds 2024 final at the O2 in London: 72 cameras, 80 transmission lines, 256 audio channels, 1,500+ on-site crew. Shows the scale from the floor, not the control room.

item.title: [recommended] Riot Games streamlines production of Valorant Champions Paris with ST 2110 flypack
item.description: SVG Europe - Riot's new IP-based flypack: tech load-in cut from two days to about four hours, around 40 feeds out to language partners, 80ms round trip to Dublin. Explains why crews are changing.

item.title: [recommended] Tech-eye view: Inside the epic remote production for LoL Worlds Finals 2024
item.description: SVG Europe - Q&A with Riot's broadcast engineering manager. What stays on site (truck, co-streamers) versus what runs from Riot's Dublin remote broadcast center, plus the automated vertical feed.

item.title: [recommended] League of Legends' unsung heroes: The magician of MSI 2023
item.description: PCGamesN - Interview with Sebastian Leathlean, stage manager for every League international event since 2017. What a stage manager does for teams and players on the day.

item.title: [recommended] Touring 101 - Life on The Road pt.1
item.description: Chris Shrom - A lighting professional explains club, theatre, arena, stadium and fly-date life, including trucks, bus calls and corporate-show waiting.

item.title: TrustFall Technology Group Transforms Las Vegas Convention Center Into Evo 2026 Esports Arena in Less Than 72 Hours
item.description: Aroluxe / TrustFall (EIN Presswire) - The Evo 2026 company release describes roughly 300 crew, a three-day build, LED walls, rigging points and the audio problem of a concrete convention hall.

item.title: Curve balls: Making the Esports World Cup production run smoothly
item.description: SVG Europe - Gravity Media on what goes wrong and gets fixed: a last-minute location change, a late call to add cinema cameras on the main stage, four stages. Useful for the 'how plans change' side.

item.title: Ingesting Live Video Streams at Global Scale
item.description: Twitch Engineering - Twitch's video ingest team on points of presence, backbone and origin data centers. Software side of getting a live stream to viewers. Read it for the pipeline, not the stage.

item.title: [recommended] Live from the Esports World Cup: Inside the production gallery
item.description: SVG Europe - Gallery-level detail: the TD's switcher setup, ATEMs for extra language and sponsor streams, 110 encoders sending about 280 streams, 10-12 live hours per stage per day.

item.title: [recommended] On the job with IATSE Local 28
item.description: Don McIntosh (NW Labor Press) - Reported day on a KISS arena build with local riggers, explaining the team above and below the deck and how touring and house crews work together.

item.title: 1,000 crew, 270 gaming PCs, 9 miles of fiber: Behind the scenes at IEM Katowice
item.description: The Next Web - ESL's IEM Katowice from a visitor's tour: the internet link feeding concurrent matches on four stages to the cloud. Dated (2017) and light, but shows the LAN-event backbone.

item.title: [recommended] Labor of love: rigger
item.description: Ben Mazuer interview (Petzl) - A working rigger talks through long setup-and-strike days, ceiling load limits, team rotation, fatigue and getting started locally.

item.title: 7 Days, Zero Sleep, Millimetric Passion: Behind the Scenes of the PMGC World Finals
item.description: Sahneva Editorial Team - A PUBG Mobile vendor account focuses on physical stage panels, LED fit, overhead rigging and cross-language coordination at the 2023 Istanbul final.

item.title: The largest VALORANT production to date and how cloud computing enabled it
item.description: Mad City - Fully distributed production crew (TD, audio, replay, graphics, observers) working from a cloud studio. Early example of the remote model Riot now runs permanently.

item.title: EVO Championship - Mastering eSports Production
item.description: Trust Fall Technology Group - An Evo vendor case study explains nine stage builds, concurrent load-ins, 3D visualization, pre-rigging and advance programming.

item.title: The Team Behind Worlds 2022 Esports Broadcast
item.description: Riot Games - Who actually staffs Worlds: people from film, TV, sports, music and live entertainment. Good for seeing what roles exist and where PA-type people come from.

item.title: [recommended] Before Doors
item.description: hob.farm - A Las Vegas house-crew account of a five-hour concert load-in after both loading elevators failed.

item.title: [recommended] Esports World Cup 2025: Inside EFG's Hybrid Production
item.description: Sports Video Group - ESL FACEIT Group's head of broadcast engineering on running multiple stages, studios and server rooms across several buildings, mixing baseband and ST 2110.

item.title: [recommended] How Riot Esports Delivers Worlds 2022 Broadcast to a Global Audience
item.description: Riot Games - The 'world feed' model: Riot builds a kit of venue footage, graphics and music, and 22 partners make 21 language shows from it. Also covers how a broadcast day starts with a story meeting days before going live.

item.title: [recommended] Let's Load in!
item.description: SoundGirls (byline not exposed in fetched article) - A touring audio lead walks through Mean Girls load-in, from truck order and cable runs to splitting the local crew and tuning the room.

item.title: How Riot used tech from The Mandalorian to build Worlds' mixed reality stage
item.description: The Verge - LED volume stage for the 2020 Shanghai Worlds, built on a compressed schedule when travel stopped. Older and consumer-press level, but a clear picture of stage tech.
